_note: Sunrise Health PPO is a fictional plan. This synthetic benefits summary exists so the demo has controllable ground truth. Structure mirrors a real Summary of Benefits and Coverage.

chunks.title: Your deductible
chunks.text: You pay the first $1,500 of allowed charges each calendar year before the plan begins sharing costs for most services. Amounts applied to the deductible count toward your out-of-pocket maximum.

chunks.title: Your coinsurance
chunks.text: After you meet the deductible, the plan pays 80% of the allowed amount for in-network care and you pay 20% coinsurance. Coinsurance is always calculated on the allowed amount, never on the provider's billed charge.

chunks.title: Your out-of-pocket maximum
chunks.text: Your out-of-pocket maximum is $6,500 per individual per year. Once your deductible, copays, and coinsurance reach $6,500, the plan pays 100% of allowed charges for covered in-network services for the rest of the year.

chunks.title: Your copays
chunks.text: Office visit copays are $25 for primary care and $50 for specialists. The emergency room copay is $250, waived if you are admitted to the hospital. Copays apply even before the deductible is met.

chunks.title: Preventive care costs you nothing in-network
chunks.text: In-network preventive services required by the Affordable Care Act, such as annual wellness visits, screening mammograms, and flu shots, are covered at 100% with no deductible, copay, or coinsurance. You should owe $0 for these services.

chunks.title: Emergency care
chunks.text: Emergency services are covered at the in-network benefit level no matter which hospital treats you. After the $250 ER copay, the plan pays 80% of the allowed amount and you pay 20% coinsurance, subject to the deductible.

chunks.title: In-network vs out-of-network
chunks.text: In-network providers accept the plan's allowed amount as payment in full, minus your share. Out-of-network providers have not agreed to our rates and may bill you the difference, except where federal or state surprise-billing protections apply.

chunks.title: Services that need approval first
chunks.text: Advanced imaging such as MRI and CT, planned inpatient admissions, and certain outpatient surgeries require prior authorization. Emergency care never requires prior authorization.
